correctness.rationale: At endemic equilibrium S=1/R and I=aJ; naturally recovered class C=J B_T(v), B_T(v)=E[(1−e^(−vT))/v], and vaccine stock V=fb from actual administered-dose flow f=v(S+C). Hence K=1−1/R−fb>0, J=K/(a+B_T(v)), and G_T(v)=v[1/R+K B/(a+B)]=f. Its derivative 1/R+K[B²+a E(T e^(−vT))]/(a+B)²>0 gives the unique positive root. For fixed hazard the third derivative of g(t)=e^(−vt) is negative: the two Hermite quadratic interpolants at (ell,u) and (d,L) yield sharp pointwise and hence Laplace bounds simultaneously for all v, with unique endpoint two-atom laws. Propagating those bounds through monotone budget equations and B(v) decreasing yields v_nu+≤v_T≤v_nu- and J_nu+≤J_T≤J_nu- (and I=aJ). Independently checked endpoint moments, unique budget roots, and ordered incidence values J_-=0.1813468073, J_middle=0.1750958197, J_+=0.1700143310 for given parameters. Only stationary equilibrium, not dynamic stability, follows.
residual_risks: Positive stationary endemic equilibria only; no proof of global attraction, transient bounds, breakthrough infections or network structure.
Atom endpoint attainment assumes general probability laws on [ell,L].

originality.rationale: Yang–Saldaña–Scoglio established the SIRVS renewal stationary equations for a fixed hazard, and Hermite two-moment inequalities are classical. This finding holds actual vaccine-dose flow fixed, recalibrates hazard for every distribution, and proves the resulting sharp incidence and prevalence envelopes. Neither inspected epidemiological theorem implies the combined fixed-dose extremizer result.

value.rationale: The actual administered vaccine-dose flow, rather than an assumed identical individual hazard, is a natural fixed policy resource; eligible population size responds to the immunity law. The theorem obtains computable sharp worst/best endemic incidence and prevalence when immunity duration is known only through support, mean and variance. The extremizers are explicit two-point laws, a meaningful information-limited optimal bound.
